assumptions: The database searched is the one the matches came from; the best match per spectrum is kept.
limits: Indistinguishable proteins are reported as a group rather than one being chosen.
A protein score aggregates peptide scores; it is not a probability (bayesian_protein_inference is that).
bio.jane/contract.question: Which proteins do these peptide-spectrum matches support, and which cannot be told apart?

description: Protein inference from peptide-spectrum matches (validated against OpenMS BasicProteinInferenceAlgorithm on PXD000001): maps each peptide to the protein database, keeps the best match per spectrum, scores each protein by aggregating its peptides' best scores, reports the proteins its evidence cannot tell apart as indistinguishable groups, and the percent of each sequence the matches cover.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

aggregation.description: how a protein's peptide scores combine: best one, mean (sum over count), or product.

chargeVariantsSeparate.description: count each charge state of a peptide as its own evidence.

coverageOf.description: the accession whose sequence coverage is drawn; empty draws the first protein of the best group, as the Coverage tab opens on.

database.description: the protein database searched, as FASTA; the accession is the header up to the first space.

greedyGroupResolution.description: razor peptides: give each shared peptide only to its best-scoring protein or group (ties to the one with more matches) and drop proteins left with no peptide of their own.

higherIsBetter.description: true for scores like HyperScore; false for e-values, q-values and PEPs.

ilEquivalent.description: treat isoleucine and leucine (and a database J) as the same residue when mapping peptides.

maxAmbiguousResidues.description: how many ambiguous database residues (B, J, Z, X) one peptide match may resolve.

minPeptides.description: report only proteins with at least this many evidences (0 reports every matched protein).

modificationVariantsSeparate.description: count each modified form of a peptide as its own evidence.

peptideProteinResolution.description: resolve shared peptides between indistinguishable groups: in each connected set of groups the highest-probability group (then the one with more peptides) takes its peptides from the rest, and each set is reported as an ambiguity group; not combined with greedyGroupResolution.

psms.description: the matches as a table with a header row naming spectrum, peptide, charge and score (tab- or comma-separated); peptides are ProForma.

scoreColumn.description: which column holds the score inference uses, when the table carries several (OpenMS score_type); a column named pep or q-value sets its own direction.

scoresArePep.description: the scores are posterior error probabilities: matches compete lowest first, and each protein combines 1 − PEP into a posterior probability (higher is better); implies higherIsBetter false.

useSharedPeptides.description: let a peptide that maps to several proteins count for each of them.

name: infer_proteins

ambiguityGroups.description: with peptide–protein resolution: one group per connected set of groups, best group first, with the best probability. Null when that resolution was not asked for, because an empty list would read as a dataset with no ambiguity in it

coverageMap.description: one protein's sequence with the peptides that identified it laid under the residues they cover, unique in blue and shared in orange: the Coverage tab's picture of `coverageOf`

groups.description: indistinguishable protein groups, best first: probability (the best member score) and accessions

method.description: the inference algorithm and mapping that produced these proteins, named

proteins.description: one row per protein: accession, score, evidences counted, sequence coverage (%)

scoreColumn.description: the column the match scores were read from, which decides whether higher or lower is better
